questions.q: In the recommended diagnostic workflow, what should be done before running any formal statistical test on a series?
options: Immediately run the Ljung-Box test
Visualize the raw series to look for obvious trend, variance changes, or structural breaks
Convert the series to log returns regardless of what it represents
Fit an ARMA model first, then test afterward
questions.explain: Visualizing the series first helps catch obvious issues like trend, variance shifts, or structural breaks that could otherwise produce misleading results from formal tests applied blindly.

questions.q: Why does the `regression` argument of statsmodels' `adfuller()` matter?
options: It has no real effect on the test's conclusions
It controls whether a constant and/or trend term is included in the test regression, and using the wrong specification on a trending series can produce misleading results
It only affects the speed of computation, not the result
It determines whether the test is one-sided or two-sided
questions.explain: The regression argument ('c', 'ct', 'n', 'ctt') controls the deterministic terms included in the ADF test regression. Testing a series with an obvious trend using the wrong specification can cause the test to misleadingly fail to reject a unit root.

questions.q: Why can a structural break (a shift in a series' mean partway through the sample) cause the ADF test to spuriously fail to reject the unit-root null?
options: Structural breaks always make a series more stationary, not less
The test can mistake the shift in regime for the kind of persistent drift characteristic of a true unit root, even though each sub-period may be genuinely stationary
ADF cannot be computed at all when a structural break is present
Structural breaks only affect the Ljung-Box test, not ADF
questions.explain: A series that is stationary within two different regimes but tested as one continuous series can appear non-stationary to the ADF test, because the regime shift mimics the kind of persistent behavior a true unit root would produce.

questions.q: What question does the Ljung-Box test answer that a single-lag look at the ACF plot does not directly answer?
options: Whether the series has a unit root
Whether the autocorrelations up to lag k, taken jointly, are statistically different from zero as a group
Whether the series is cointegrated with another series
Whether the series follows a Normal distribution
questions.explain: Ljung-Box tests a joint null hypothesis — that all autocorrelations up to lag k are simultaneously zero — rather than examining each lag individually as the ACF plot does.

questions.q: A model's residuals pass the ADF stationarity test, show a clean ACF/PACF, and pass Ljung-Box with no leftover structure. What can be concluded?
options: The model is guaranteed to have genuine forecasting skill and needs no further validation
These diagnostics confirm the model's statistical assumptions are reasonably met, but they do not by themselves guarantee good out-of-sample forecasting performance or economic sense
The model cannot possibly be overfit
No further testing of any kind is necessary
questions.explain: Passing statistical diagnostics is necessary but not sufficient. A model can satisfy all of these checks and still perform poorly out-of-sample or lack real economic meaning, so out-of-sample validation remains essential.
